paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.
model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the percentage of matches between large language model (LLM) judgments and human annotations for six categories: No Hallucination, Oriented, Active, Self-aware, Rigorous, and Correct. The categories are displayed on the vertical axis, listed in that order from top to bottom, with no apparent sorting. The horizontal axis represents percentage values, with a linear scale ranging from 0% to 100%, with tick marks every 20%. Each category has two adjacent horizontal bars representing “Matched” and “Not Matched” percentages, visually differentiated by blue and white colors respectively. For "No Hallucination", the “Matched” bar extends to 98.33% and the “Not Matched” bar extends to 1.67%. The remaining categories show "Matched" values of 97.33%, 97.00%, 94.00%, 95.33%, and 99.00% combined with "Not Matched" values of 2.67%, 3.00%, 6.00%, 4.67%, and 1.00% respectively. All bars are of consistent width spanning the full range of percentage values, and none are visually emphasized with shading or outlines. A legend clarifies the color mapping for “Matched” and “Not Matched” status.
